question.text: Water in a river flows horizontally to the right at a constant speed of 2 m/s between two parallel banks. A person starts rowing from point A on the lower bank to reach point B on the upper bank. The straight line connecting A to B makes an angle of 45° with the downstream bank. If the speed of the boat relative to the water is 4 m/s, find the angle θ with the perpendicular to the river bank at which the boat should be steered.
conditions: river flow speed v_r = 2 m/s downstream (to the right)
speed of boat relative to water |v_br| = 4 m/s
target path AB makes an angle of 45° with the bank downstream
resultant velocity of the boat is along line AB
angle θ is measured relative to the normal to the bank towards downstream

figure.description: A horizontal river with parallel banks where the current flows to the right at 2 m/s. Point A is located on the bottom bank and point B on the top bank such that the straight line AB is inclined at 45° to the horizontal river bank. A dashed line normal to the banks extends upward from point A. The boat's heading makes an angle θ to the right of this vertical dashed normal.

solution.approach: Write the resultant of the boat's velocity and the river's velocity, and require it to point along AB, which makes 45° with both the bank and the perpendicular.

steps.text: Let x be across the river along the perpendicular and y be along the bank; the boat is rowed at angle θ from the x-axis, tilted toward the flow.
Since AB makes 45° with the bank, it also makes 45° with the perpendicular, so the resultant's x and y components must be equal.

steps.equation: 4cos θ − 4sin θ = 2 → cos θ − sin θ = 0.5

steps.text: Solve this trigonometric equation for θ between 0° and 90°.

final_answer.value: θ ≈ 24.3° from the perpendicular to the bank, tilted toward the direction of flow

common_mistakes.text: Ignoring the effect of the current and rowing straight along AB, taking θ = 45°.
Swapping the sine and cosine terms while writing the resultant components, 4sin θ − 4cos θ = 2, which gives the wrong angle θ ≈ 65.7°.
